The new RNN wins this conditional test

Experimental checkpoint; current default retained. Provider-generated labels cover only parts of the match. These scores do not establish official challenge accuracy.

Test: Real Madrid–Barcelona, 1 March 2020. Three training matches, PSG–Marseille validation; test labels opened only after selection and freeze.

295 provider-labelled reference spells. The candidate predicts 179, so under-segmentation remains unresolved. The target of 0.8–0.9 has not been reached.

Selected model

One recurrent layer, 24 units, iteration 5, decoder penalty 48. Two layers and later iterations did not improve validation spell F1. Dropout, L2 and clipped gradients were used. Candidate trained from scratch on top-five-league matches only.

Limitations

  • Automatically generated provider labels; this is a weak-supervision transfer experiment.
  • Only observed H/A-labelled runs are scored; no supervised dead-ball state.
  • Unknown gaps fragment spells and can inflate F1: these scores do not establish the official challenge target.
  • Training checkpoint selected repeatedly on one validation match; one test match is limited evidence.
  • Interpolated 25 Hz frames are not independent observations.
  • Offline decoder uses future evidence; not live forecasting.
  • Existing current comparator has second-division training ancestry; new candidate trained from scratch only on selected top-five-league matches.
